sub_answers.text: He severed relations with the UWFi after the promotion began moving away from its shootfighting style and favoring performers over wrestlers, taking his old NWA championship belt back with him [d668815s10p0]. He specifically criticized the promotion's use of power bombs as unrealistic despite their later adoption in MMA and his own prior use of them [d668815s10p0]. He publicly described modern professional wrestling as "choreographed tumbling" and was highly critical of its lack of actual wrestling skills [d668815s10p0].

sub_answers.text: He was a former top-level competitor who, after retiring, became a special guest referee, promoter and trainer, providing practical professional experience relevant to training and production work [d668815s10p0]. He served as the commissioner and occasional trainer for the shoot-style promotion UWFi and taught catch-wrestling techniques there, including spending one week every month in Japan instructing wrestlers [d668815s10p0]. He conducted coaching seminars in Virginia and Florida and maintained active mentoring relationships with notable figures such as his student Gene LeBell and associations with Gokor Chivichyan and LeBell's Hayastan MMA Academy [d668815s10p0]. He also remained involved in amateur wrestling, attended collegiate events, and held leadership roles (e.g., president of the Cauliflower Alley Club and board membership for the George Tragos/Lou Thesz Hall of Fame), which provided informal qualifications and industry standing for his training and production roles [d668815s10p0].
